paper_style.palette_strategy: Figure 1 uses categorical module fills; Figure 2 uses five fixed line/marker colors; Figures 3–4 reuse blue/lilac categorical bars. Tables are monochrome booktabs with bold best cells only in the main result tables. Chart colors have some marker/position redundancy but are not consistently grayscale-safe.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: The PDF figures and tables render as vector paths/text; Figure 1's public counterpart is a PNG rendered asset, but the PDF object itself contains vector diagram elements. Tables are vector text and rules.
paper_style.style_consistency: The paper maintains a restrained single-column serif/booktabs visual language, with full-width figures and centered appendix tables. Main result captions are more explanatory than appendix hyperparameter captions; color keys and uncertainty reporting are incomplete across figures.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: The overall framework of our In-Place Test-Time Training. The module operates sequentially on input chunks. For each chunk, the current fast weights are first applied to the intermediate activations Z to produce the output. Then, these weights are updated using the activations Z and a value V derived from the token embeddings. This ”apply-then-update” cycle allows the model to dynamically adapt to incoming context in a strictly causal manner.

color.semantic_mapping: Fills identify Attention, Gated Linear Layer, fast-weight/loss boxes, chunk/update blocks, input/value/output streams, and the generating-direction arrow; text and grouping boundaries are black.

encodings.x: left-to-right processing path from input embedding through Attention and Gated Linear Layer to MLP with In-Place TTT
encodings.y: vertical generating direction and fast-weight state progression
encodings.shape: rounded module boxes, circular additions, stacked token/chunk blocks, and dotted grouping frames
encodings.line: solid arrows show data/update flow; dotted frames and dashed state guide show grouping/causal stages
encodings.text: component names, Wdown states, loss, ΔW, Apply/Update, and Conv1D & Projection

figures.data_and_statistics: No statistical data are plotted. The diagram encodes the strictly causal apply-then-update cycle for input chunks: current Wdown is applied to Z to produce O, then Z and V-derived targets update Wdown; p.6–p.7 explain the context-parallel prefix scan and boundary handling.
figures.evidence_relation: Method-interface/theory-mechanism object linking the Wdown in-place design in §3.1, the LM-aligned target in §3.2, and the parallel-scan implementation in §3.4. It is the visual entry point for the Q1–Q3 experiments.
design_strengths: Outer and inner dotted frames distinguish the existing Transformer path from the in-place MLP fast-weight process.
The Apply and Update stages are explicit and ordered, while state superscripts expose the transition across chunks.
Arrow direction, labels, and box structure provide redundancy beyond color.
design_weaknesses: Many arrows and state boxes compete for attention and require backtracking between Wdown, ΔW, V, and the loss.
No legend defines the categorical fills, and pale fills lose hierarchy in grayscale.
The caption omits tensor dimensions, CP abbreviation, and document-boundary reset.
figures.reusable_pattern: Place the frozen backbone, adaptable state, apply/update stages, and parallel aggregation in one directed diagram, using nested frames to show a new mechanism embedded inside an existing block.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: Sliding Window Perplexity at varying context lengths on the Pile dataset for 500M (left) and 1.5B (right) parameter models. Our In-Place TTT consistently achieves lower perplexity than all competitive baselines.

color.semantic_mapping: Each method has a fixed line/marker color: In-Place TTT, SWA, GLA, Deltanet, and LaCT. Marker shapes and the repeated legend provide redundancy; the five muted colors remain difficult to separate in grayscale.

encodings.x: context length, shown as 2k, 4k, 8k, 16k, and 32k on a log2-style axis
encodings.shape: method-specific markers (circle, square, diamond, triangle-up, triangle-down)
encodings.text: panel titles, axis labels, tick labels, and per-panel method legends

figures.data_and_statistics: Validation perplexity is evaluated on a fixed final token block while preceding context is extended; p.9 identifies Pile and Proof-Pile-2 validation for the from-scratch evaluation. Curves cover 2k–32k context and show no repeats, intervals, error bands, or failure markers. In-Place TTT decreases through the full context range, while SWA in the 1.5B panel plateaus after 4k.
figures.evidence_relation: Headline/main-comparison evidence for Q2. Figure 2 is introduced in §4.2 and its lower perplexity curves are interpreted on p.9 as evidence that the mechanism compresses and uses incoming context.
design_strengths: The two model scales use the same axis semantics and five-method visual grammar, enabling a direct shape comparison.
Markers plus a legend make overlapping method curves traceable.
The full context trajectory communicates behavior that a single endpoint table would hide.
design_weaknesses: The caption does not define the fixed final block, context sampling, log-scale choice, or repetitions.
No uncertainty band or run variability is shown, so small separations cannot be audited.
Five muted lines and small legends become difficult to distinguish when printed or downsampled.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use matched model panels with a fixed method color/marker mapping for context-scaling curves, and define the evaluation block, axis transform, and repetition protocol in the caption.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.module: ablation / state, chunk, and objective choices

caption.text: Figure 3: Ablation studies on the key design choices of the In-Place TTT framework, evaluated on the RULER benchmark with a 1.7B parameter model. The plots illustrate the impact of: (a) State size, showing that performance improves as the state size scales; (b) Chunk size, demonstrating a performance trade-off where intermediate sizes (e.g., 512, 1024) are optimal; and (c) The LM-Aligned Value objective, confirming that both the convolution (w Conv) and the projection (w Proj) are crucial.

color.semantic_mapping: Variant series are distinguished by a reused ordered blue/gray palette: state-size variants in panel (a), chunk sizes in (b), and Conv/Proj objective variants in (c). Heights encode Score and legends define the series.

encodings.color: state-size, chunk-size, or LM-aligned objective variant, depending on panel
encodings.facet: (a) State size; (b) Chunk size; (c) LM-Aligned Objective
encodings.text: panel titles, variant legends, axis labels, and category ticks

figures.data_and_statistics: The 1.7B-parameter model is evaluated on RULER. Panel (a) compares 4×, 1×, and 0.5× state size; panel (b) compares C=256, 512, 1024, and 2048; panel (c) compares w Conv, Proj; w/o Conv; w/o Proj; and w/o Conv, Proj. No exact bar values, repeats, uncertainty, or error bars are printed.
figures.evidence_relation: Ablation/mechanism evidence for Q3. The panels map to §3.1 chunk updates and §3.2 Conv1D/Wtarget design, and p.10 explicitly connects panel (c) to the theoretical LM-aligned objective.
design_strengths: Three design questions share a common RULER context axis and score orientation.
Complete per-panel legends keep variant membership visible despite the compact layout.
The caption states the model, benchmark, variant families, and directional findings.
design_weaknesses: No direct numeric labels or variability are shown, making exact effect sizes unavailable from the figure.
Legends and ticks are small after compression to the full-width panel strip.
The repeated blue/lightness palette is not grayscale-safe and the baseline configuration is implicit.
figures.reusable_pattern: Split a multi-part ablation into aligned panels with the same task axis, retain complete variant legends, and bind each variant family to a method component in the caption.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4: Efficiency analysis of In-Place TTT. Both prefill throughput (a, b) and peak memory (c, d) metrics are presented for 4B models with Sliding-Window Attention (SWA) and Full Attention at various context lengths. Our In-Place TTT introduces negligible overhead in practical scenarios.

color.semantic_mapping: Within each panel, light and slightly darker blue bars identify Baseline and TTT; panel titles identify SWA versus Full Attention. The legend is the only explicit key.

encodings.y: Prefill TPS (K tokens/s) in panels (a,b); Peak Memory (GB) in panels (c,d)
encodings.facet: Throughput/Memory × SWA/Full Attention in four panels
encodings.text: panel titles, axis labels, tick labels, and per-panel two-item legends

figures.data_and_statistics: Four panels contain 24 bars: Baseline/TTT at 8k, 32k, and 128k for throughput under SWA and Full Attention, and peak memory under the same two attention settings. Appendix D.2 states batch size 1 and Nvidia H800 inference. No repeats, error bars, or uncertainty are shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Efficiency-cost evidence for the implementation claim. Figure 4 follows Table 3 and §4.3, linking the CP/chunk-wise implementation to measured throughput and memory overhead at 4B scale.
design_strengths: A 2×2 small-multiple structure separates speed from memory and SWA from Full Attention.
All panels share the same three context levels, making overhead trends easy to scan.
Short legends and direct panel titles keep the comparison surface compact.
design_weaknesses: No direct values, relative overhead percentages, error bars, or timing repetitions are shown.
The caption does not state batch size, H800 hardware, measurement window, or peak-memory definition.
The light/dark blue distinction depends on color/legend and is weak in grayscale.
figures.reusable_pattern: Show throughput and memory as matched small multiples across system modes and context levels, while defining hardware, batch, timing window, and repeat aggregation at the figure boundary.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 establishes the in-place architecture and causal update cycle; Tables 1–2 test pre-trained drop-in and cross-model extension; Figure 2 and Table 3 cover from-scratch perplexity and 4B downstream/long-context comparison; Figure 3 isolates state/chunk/objective mechanisms; Figure 4 measures throughput/memory; Tables 4–8 supply training-stage, budget, and architecture reproduction details.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Figure 1–4 captions give setup and, especially for Figures 2–4, explicit directional findings. Tables 1–3 define benchmark/unit or abbreviations, while Tables 4–8 are largely title-only; none of the table captions defines seeds, repeats, or uncertainty.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Main tables use grouped headers and model/method row groups: evaluation regimes in Table 1, model/method in Table 2, task families in Table 3. Appendix Tables 4–8 use parameter rows with model or stage columns and occasional horizontal semantic separators.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 1 maps §3.1–§3.4 mechanisms to the implementation; Tables 1–2 answer Q1; Figure 2/Table 3 answer Q2; Figure 3 answers Q3 mechanism choices; Figure 4 tests efficiency, with Tables 4–8 fixing the settings needed to interpret the results.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main figures/tables state performance and ablation outcomes, while Appendix D Tables 4–8 and Algorithm 1 p.18 supply training budgets, model dimensions, continual stages, and CP implementation details. The appendix supports reproduction but does not contain figure/table generation sources.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Body, captions, and tables use Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern; Figure 1 embeds Arial and Cambria Math for the diagram, and Figures 2–4 use Times New Roman. Table header bolding is stable for results and hyperparameter tables, with chart legends/ticks substantially smaller than captions.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Tables are black/white and grayscale-safe. Figures 2–4 reuse blue or muted gray-blue palettes, while Figure 1 uses role-specific categorical fills. Figure 2's markers and Figure 1's labels add redundancy, but bar palettes and lightness differences remain color-dependent.

most_reusable_patterns: Nested architecture diagram with explicit apply/update state transitions and causal arrows.
Matched model panels for sliding-window context curves with fixed method color/marker mapping.
Aligned multi-panel ablation with a shared task axis and per-panel variant legends.
Stage/model-column appendix tables that separate training schedules from architectural dimensions.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1 is the strongest method-interface object because it makes the in-place Wdown state and apply-then-update semantics traceable.
Figure 2 is the clearest Q2 headline comparison because it exposes the complete context-length trajectory for two model scales.
Figure 3 is the highest-value mechanism object because each panel maps a design choice to a RULER score pattern.
Table 3 is the densest decision surface, combining common-sense and long-context performance for 4B variants.
failure_patterns: Appendix hyperparameter captions are title-only and leave shared scope, units, hardware, seeds, and repetition outside the table boundary.
Figures 2–4 have no uncertainty/repeat encoding, and small legends/ticks reduce single-page readability.
Color/lightness channels are not uniformly keyed or grayscale-safe; Figure 1 has no color legend despite many categorical fills.
Only a related pipeline PNG is public; exact vector figure sources for Figure 1 and all Figure 2–4/table generators are absent.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper uses a restrained serif/booktabs system to move from an in-place TTT architecture through context curves, downstream comparisons, mechanism ablations, and efficiency costs, but its visual evidence would be more auditable with complete generation sources, caption-level protocols, and uncertainty/repetition metadata.
